channel.title: Sextant
channel.description: Updates for Sextant, a business's data warehouse native on the Mac.

item.title: Version 0.1.0
item.description:
The first release.

Sextant keeps a business's data on its own Mac. It syncs from the databases, files and services you already have into a local DuckDB warehouse, models that data with SQL you own, and answers questions about it in plain words — every figure shown with the query behind it. Nothing leaves the machine unless you publish it somewhere yourself.

What it does:

  • Syncs from PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, DuckDB, MongoDB, BigQuery, Google Sheets, CSV, Parquet, JSON and Excel files, and object storage (S3, R2, GCS, MinIO), Delta Lake and Iceberg included — through an SSH tunnel where the server sits behind a bastion.
  • Copies a large table a range of its key at a time, so a cancel, a failure or a quit resumes rather than starts again.
  • Models the data with dbt-shaped SQL files you own, built as a graph with tests that gate whatever reads them. Claude proposes the staging, core and mart models for what you have synced.
  • Keeps a field guide: what each table and column means, what one row is, which rows every answer should leave out, and what a coded column's values stand for. The warehouse works out much of it by itself, and Sextant can read the codebase that wrote the data for the rest, checking every meaning against your own rows before offering it.
  • Writes those meanings into SQL, so a status reads "done" everywhere downstream rather than 4.
  • Answers questions in plain words, with the queries and charts behind them, and tells you when a figure in an answer was worked out rather than queried.
  • Lets you write SQL yourself in Explore, with Claude's help when you want it.
  • Pins what matters to a dashboard, and says when a figure is unlike its own history.
  • Runs questions on a schedule as briefings, and exports any answer as a PDF.
  • Says something in Slack when an answer is wrong: no orders since this morning, a store under its floor, a load that never landed. It speaks when something changes and stays quiet while it stays changed.
  • Keeps every project fresh on its own schedule with no window open, from the menu bar.
  • Publishes what you build to PostgreSQL, MySQL, BigQuery, Google Sheets or files, keeps the warehouse itself as a DuckLake in your own bucket if you want it there, and lets Claude Code and other assistants read it read-only over MCP.

Requires macOS 26. Signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple.

Sextant is a codename and the app is early: expect rough edges, and please report what you find.
